text: In Kazakhstan, most people dream of buying, because owning a flat feels like security for the family. Renting makes more sense for young people who might move for work, since it's flexible and doesn't tie you to a mortgage for twenty years. So I'd say rent while your life is changing, and buy once you know where you want to settle.

questions.followUp: What do most people in your country do?
questions.question: Is it better to rent or to buy a home?

text: Mainly because housing is so expensive. Even with a decent salary, it can take years to save for a deposit, and rent eats up a big part of young people's income. In our culture it's also completely normal, especially until marriage, so there's less pressure to leave. The downside is that some people become independent quite late, for example in managing money or running a home.

questions.question: Why do many young people still live with their parents?

text: Some will, especially now that many jobs can be done remotely. If you only need to go to the office once a week, living an hour away becomes realistic, and houses are much cheaper there. But villages need good internet, schools and hospitals first; without them, families won't move. So it depends a lot on government investment in rural areas.

questions.question: Will more people move from cities to the countryside in the future?

text: The main advantage is that it's usually cheaper and closer to shops, schools and transport than a house. You also get great views from the upper floors. On the negative side, you have less privacy, noise from neighbours can be a problem, and in some older buildings the lifts break down regularly. And, of course, there's no garden, which matters a lot to families with children.

questions.question: What are the advantages and disadvantages of living in a high-rise apartment block?

text: I think it should, because a stable home is the basis for starting a family and a career. In Kazakhstan there are already programmes with low-interest mortgages, and they've helped many people. However, the queues are very long, and the flats are often built far from jobs and schools. Quality and location matter as much as quantity, otherwise people simply won't want to live there.
